column4: Owner 2026-07-24: "I am considering changing the product-weighted indices of industrial production for value-weighted, which is the norm in economics." Correct as to weighting, with one clarification carried into the build: the norm is value-added WEIGHTS applied to VOLUME indices (ONS IoP, Destatis Produktionsindex, NBS all do this), NOT output measured in value. Measuring in value would import global commodity price cycles unrelated to domestic electricity policy, and would let an energy-cost margin squeeze register as falling output — the mechanism under test, which would compromise the falsifiability rule. COMMON rather than country-specific weights chosen by the owner so the composite stays a like-for-like basket; country-specific GVA shares are the stricter norm but would stop the three indices measuring the same thing. EU27 is the workable "advanced economy" proxy — verified that NO OECD-wide aggregate exists in SDBS, STAN or National Accounts (49 individual countries, zero zone codes; US absent at 4-digit). 2010 base matches the index base and sits within 1.7pp of the pooled 2008-2023 mean on every component. Equal weights (D65) were themselves adopted only because electricity weighting (D37) was contestable on efficiency/route-mix grounds; value weights carry no such problem, so this is a progression rather than a reversal.

column3: LINE LOSSES ADDED TO THE UK BUILD; DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED TO GERMANY. The UK E1/E2 stacks now carry a loss gross-up on the energy purchase: TLM 1.008 for all archetypes (Elexon BSC Section T), times LLF 1.000 large / 1.024 medium (HV, Northern Powergrid Annex 5). column3: CCL RE-BASING — LIKE-FOR-LIKE ON BOTH SIDES, AND THE MINERALOGICAL/METALLURGICAL EXEMPTION MODELLED. Owner-approved 2026-07-26 after owner asked 'so firms can be exempted from the CCL?' and observed that a like-for-like comparison must include CCL on both the observed and modelled side or exclude it on both. THREE CHANGES: (1) OBSERVED re-based from QEP table 3.4.1 (excl CCL) to 3.4.2 (INCL CCL) for both bands — stage4_uk r51/r52, flowing to timeseries r20/r30/r78/r79. Rationale: CCL is NOT recoverable, so the Eurostat X_VAT basis used for Germany (which includes the Stromsteuer) corresponds to 3.4.2, not 3.4.1; the previous pairing compared an excl-tax UK observed line against an incl-tax UK stack AND against an incl-tax German observed line. (2) E2 CCL SET TO ZERO: mineralogical and metallurgical processes are EXEMPT from the CCL main rates (HMRC Excise Notice CCL1/3 s3.14 + Annex A, from 01.04.2014) — this covers the steel, aluminium and cement archetypes on which the study's output index is built. timeseries r19/r29 lose their +CCL term; the 32 E2 CCL rows in data_lineitems return 0. A non-min/met EII (e.g. paper) would pay 8% of the main rate under a CCA (92% electricity discount, gov.uk CCL rates) — FLAGGED, NOT MODELLED, so E2 is a floor for such firms. (3) WEDGE/GATES SIMPLIFIED: the 32 memo rows drop their '-CCL' correction (obs - (E1 - CCL) -> obs - E1) and the validation gates compare plain obs vs [E2, E1]; the D68 'UK CCL-consistent' basis is retired as no longer needed. SUPERSEDES the CCL clause of D68 and the D29 assumption that UK CCA coverage is unpublishable — see Q98: the 3.4.2-minus-3.4.1 difference MEASURES the relief actually taken across the band (19% of the main rate in 2010 rising to 91% in 2021, 58% in 2025), banked timeseries r132-134.
